Problem: Read the following context and choose the correct option to answer the question. Context: The power of veto lies with the President of India under Article 78 of Indian Constitution. These include : Election Commission ; Union Public Service Commission ; Finance Commission ; Auditor General Of India Etc. In addition to above mentioned constitutional bodies, Parliament has enacted several statutes creating various bodies / authorities such as Central Bureau Of Investigation CBI ; Securities Exchange Board SEBI ; Competition Commission OF India CCI And Reserve Bank RBI Etc. All these statutory authorities enjoy autonomy in exercise of powers vested in them under law. For example RBI Act provides immunity against legal process including court proceedings except when authorized by central Government. Similarly Securities Contract Regulation Act confers immunity to members of Sebi Against disclosure of information related to investigation unless required by competent Court Or Tribunal OR ordered By Govt On National Security Grounds. Thus apart From Constitutional Bodies Several Statutory Authorities Have Been Created Which Enjoy Autonomy While Exercising Their Powers Vested Under Law Question: How does the president exercise power?
